measurements.note: Corrected against the source: the sheet states how its test bars were made, once for the table: "Testing Specimen Printing Conditions:". Flagged physically implausible: the sheet prints a heat deflection of 200 °C at 0.455 MPa on printed bars and states no treatment, and advises drying the part "in the oven at 120-130°C for 6-8 hours to increase the strength of the model" (p. 3). PET prints glassy, fibre-filled or not (D158, D176): a 15 % glass-fibre PET bar that was not crystallised deflects near 80 °C (Polymaker Fiberon PET-GF15, 81.6 °C as printed and 133.7 °C annealed), and Flashforge's own PET-CF of the same LEHVOSS compound family prints 100 °C "not annealed". 200 °C is a crystallised bar's, annealed or printed hot, which the page does not say this was. Kept as printed; it backs nothing.
